title: Turn-boundary freshness pull (inject channel deltas each turn, not just at SessionStart)

story.as_a: coding agent in a long-running session
story.i_want_to: receive NEW channel posts from other sessions at each turn, not only at SessionStart
story.so_that: when a session on another machine posts mid-way through my long session, I see it at my next turn instead of never

rationale: SessionStart injection (US-39.6) only fires once. A long session (like a big review) would never see a heads-up posted by another machine an hour in. This is the near-realtime-for-agents mechanism from the design (§5): a per-turn pull of the delta is the finest granularity an agent can actually consume — capturing all the value a websocket could, with no persistent connection and no fight with Fly suspend.

background.reference: docs/repo-coordination-bus.md §3.3, §5; claude-config hooks (UserPromptSubmit or Stop hook); reuse US-39.6's injection-safety wholesale
background.includes: A UserPromptSubmit hook pulls channel_recent(since=last_seen) and injects only new posts; last_seen persisted per session.

acceptance_criteria.description: A claude-config hook (UserPromptSubmit preferred) pulls channel_recent(project_id, since=<last-seen-for-this-session>) each turn and injects ONLY posts newer than the last pull, from OTHER sessions, as a compact TEAM CHANNEL update.
It persists a per-(session, project) last-seen high-watermark (the newest inserted_at it has injected) so the same post is never re-injected turn after turn.

It inherits US-39.6's untrusted-content hardening EXACTLY (jq-encoded bodies, fenced + truncated, off-switch-aware: CLAUDE_MEMORY / .claude/memory-off / CLAUDE_TEAM_CHANNEL=0). CRITICAL, sharper than SessionStart: a UserPromptSubmit hook that exits non-zero or emits decision:block ERASES the user's submitted prompt. This hook must ALWAYS exit 0 and NEVER block — a capture/network failure must silently produce no injection, never lose the prompt.

Silent when there are no new other-session posts (the common case). UserPromptSubmit's default timeout is 30s (not 600s), so the network calls MUST be backgrounded with a wall-clock kill / tight cumulative --max-time budget well under 30s — a slow/hung loopctl can never delay or drop the turn.

test_cases.name: new other-session post appears next turn
expected_results: the new post is injected once

test_cases.name: already-seen posts are not re-injected
preconditions: a post already injected last turn
expected_results: that post is NOT re-injected (high-watermark advanced)

test_cases.name: quiet channel adds no block and is fast
expected_results: no injection, returns within the per-turn budget

test_cases.name: malicious body is inert (inherited hardening)
preconditions: a new post with a shell-injection body
expected_results: inert text, no execution, valid output

technical_notes: Repo: claude-config. Prefer UserPromptSubmit (fires each user turn) over Stop; confirm the event provides session_id + a place to inject context.
Persist last-seen in a small per-session file (e.g. ~/.claude/.team-channel-seen-<session>) or reuse a scratch location; key by (session, project).

Factor US-39.6's render/escape/off-switch/timeout logic into a shared hook helper — and PARAMETERIZE hookEventName (session-start.sh:317-319 hardcodes "SessionStart"; this hook must emit hookSpecificOutput with hookEventName "UserPromptSubmit").

Seed the per-turn watermark (AC-40.3.2) from the SessionStart injection time so the first turn doesn't re-inject what SessionStart just showed. Intra-session races are a non-issue (UserPromptSubmit fires serially, blocking the turn); cross-session isolation is the per-session watermark file.
Keep it CHEAP: a single since-filtered call; background it with a wall-clock kill so a slow network never delays the turn.
